newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia PM warns against fake rebel defectors.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia PM warns against fake rebel defectors.

text.p: Cambodian Second Prime Minister Hun Sen on Tuesday warned against criminals trying to join the security forces by posing as Khmer Rouge defectors.

"I urge all authorities to beware of armed robbers pretending to be underground Khmer Rouge agents. We can't integrate fake Khmer Rouge or armed robbers," the premier said at a ceremony welcoming 271 rebel agents to the government side.
Hundreds of alleged underground Khmer Rouge agents, who lived as ordinary citizens, have joined the government since November under the protection of rival co-Premiers Hun Sen and Prince Norodom.

Hun Sen, who fought alongside the Khmer Rouge in the 1970s, also called on two former friends, including his former military commander Sok Saroeun, to quit the dwindling ranks of the Maoist-inspired guerrilla movement and join the government.
"I would like to appeal through television and radio to my two former friends Sok Tun and Sok Saroeun, who are now in Khmer Rouge Division 920, to please come back and join the government," he said.
The premier said Sok Tun had been a colleague of his in the 1979-93 socialist government that ruled Cambodia against an alliance of the Khmer Rouge and non-communist factions.
"Sok Saroeun was my former commander and also my friend," he said, without specifying when the two had been colleagues.

Hun Sen has denied claims that he was a former Khmer Rouge officer, saying he fought the 1970-75 Lon Nol republic after answering a call to arms by Norodom Sihanouk, who was ousted by a coup in 1970 and then formed an alliance with the guerrilla forces.
The Khmer Rouge took power in 1975 and launched a rule of terror that left more than one million people dead from execution, starvation, disease or overwork.
Hun Sen fled to Vietnam in 1977 and was picked by Hanoi as one of the leaders of the government put in place after Vietnamese troops ousted the Khmer Rouge in 1979.
The Khmer Rouge have been crippled by thousands of defections since early August, leaving an estimated 2,000 at most in their northern stronghold of Anlong Veng near the Thai border.
